post_content:
Came to know about the news about fee hike for M Tech in IITs in order to
reduce dropouts I can tell this move can do more bad than good. A student who
will dropout, will any ways drop out - higher fee paid may not deter him. The
general reasons for dropout are as follows Most programs aren't as rosy as
depicted. Only 15-20 % of M tech courses receive good placements. M Tech from
Metallurgy, Bio Tech or many other niche subjects suffer a lot for getting a
decent job. They drop out for better career opportunities if they realize it
earlier Ways to reduce dropout : 1 Get industry relevant curriculum and
special focus for placements of M Techs across the streams. The current
placement focus has been predominantly for B Tech 2 Scrap the courses/ Reduce
the intake which have seen higher dropout, lesser placements - what's the
point in enrolling in a course which doesn't have jobs in market ? Whom are
they benefiting 3 Ask students to pay a fine/fee when they dropout from the
course to compensate for opportunity loss For more than 50 years, IIT's were
more bachelor programs oriented institutes. Time to boost Masters and PhD
programs for better outcome for country.

profile_headline: Program Manager @Google. Follow me for posts on Machine Learning, Productivity & Self-Improvement
post_content:
Not using Cloud & Libraries for Machine Learning is like bringing a stone to a
gunfight. Machine Learning is all the rage now. And with the help of tools
provided by cloud computing service providers and libraries open-sourced by
multiple companies, currently, we shouldn't be reinventing the wheel. We
should be learning to use the wheel. Libraries like Scikit-learn, Tensorflow,
Keras, Pytorch and a few more are becoming the standard way of doing machine
learning. Choose library 1 for Machine Learning and 1 for Deep Learning
(choose one which is simple and popular both), and master it end to end.
Machine Learning is not about only modeling, rather all the steps from Data
Collection to ML Model deployment are part of Machine Learning.. Learn to use
the tools and build end to end solutions.. Tools are not a substitute for
expertise. Tools are not meant as a BlackBox but as an Aid. Learn to use the
tools effectively, not blindly. Otherwise, it's like using Thor's hammer to
hit a nail. Even the best tools are useless if we don't know how to use them.
